recommendations.summary: CALIBRATION PROBE -- test the load-bearing assumption under the entire discretionary sizer: that the model's stated probability means anything. Kelly is f*=(pb-q)/b, so if p is noise the sizer is not aggressive or conservative, it is ARBITRARY. Checked 2026-07-31: the desk had ZERO resolved forecasts. Not few -- zero. The most consequential input to the money path had never been scored on anything, and both trading sleeves were built to consume it. Calibration is a property of the FORECASTER, not of the strategy, so it is measurable TODAY with questions that resolve from public price data in hours: no capital, no venue keys, ~50 forecasts in two days at the cost of quota alone. Poses 6 directional questions every 6h on the sleeve's own instruments -- the same KIND of judgement it makes when trading, so the measured calibration transfers -- and resolves anything due from real bars. Pre-committed verdict: Brier >= 0.25 (the score of always answering 50%) means REMOVE the Kelly sizer and run flat size, because sizing on a meaningless number is strictly worse than not sizing on it.

recommendations.summary: 2-OF-3 ENSEMBLE CONSENSUS on the conviction sleeve -- buy hit rate with frequency. Correct only because of WHERE the hit rate sits: cost-adjusted breakeven is 31.1pct and the plausible rate is on top of it, so g per trade is tiny and small precision gains multiply it (32->33pct is x3.5 on g, 32->36pct is x11) while halving the trade count costs a factor of 2. Through the honest haircuts: no filter 33pct/460 = 34pct CAGR; 2-of-3 at 36pct/230 = 58pct; at 38pct/230 = 95pct. Three reads framed DIFFERENTLY (straight / argue the opposite side / assume your instinct is already priced) because three samples of one framing correlate and their agreement means nothing. 2-of-3 not unanimity, which cuts to ~1/4 the trades for +8pp and measures 63pct against 95pct. Consensus takes the LOWEST probability among agreeing reads since Kelly is convex in p. The rejected minority is KEPT so whether the filter helps stays measurable -- if agreement-filtered calls do not out-hit unfiltered ones, the filter goes.

recommendations.summary: 'Surpass me' had nothing measuring it. The desk benchmarks every sleeve against unlevered buy-and-hold because a levered sleeve that merely tracks the index takes risk for nothing (L1.6); by the same logic a discretionary machine that merely matches the human method it was built to copy is engineering for nothing, and nothing computed that. run_principal_benchmark re-prices the desk's OWN closed trades at the principal's demonstrated 10% risk fraction -- same calls, entries, stops and exits, only size changes -- so the difference is attributable to sizing policy alone. EXACT rather than simulated: cost in R is size-independent, so net_R = equity_return/risk_fraction and the outcome scales linearly with f. Reports RUIN rather than computing around a sequence-ending trade. VERDICT IS NOT FOREGONE and that is the point: at ~33% hit the desk's cap wins, at ~46% his 10% wins and the cap is costing growth -- verified both directions by test. SCOPE LIMIT STATED IN THE ARTIFACT: this compares SIZING POLICY on the desk's own calls; it does NOT show the machine beats the principal, because his SELECTION is unmeasured (the desk has seen one of his trades). The output also carries where the machine should win (independent bets, consistency, measurement) and where the human still does (selection, 6R winner shape) -- both halves, not the flattering one.
recommendations.reason: run_principal_benchmark re-prices the desk's own closed trades at his 10% risk; exact via size-independent net_R; RUIN reported not computed around; verdict verified to flip at the crossover in both directions; scope limit and both-sides ledger stated in the artifact; 6 tests

recommendations.summary: The desk DETECTED coma well and TREATED nothing. check_exploration reported the family DARK, check_organ_liveness separated NEVER-PRODUCED from STALE, check_miner_runway watched the seats -- three organs reported dark for days, every report correct, and no treatment was ever attempted. Detection without treatment is a monitor, not a hospital, and a ward whose alarms nobody answers gets its alarms switched off (L1.43). organ_catchup was the closest thing and is deliberately narrow: it re-fires QUOTA-KILLED organs only, one per tick, across six seats, so an organ dark from never being scheduled, from expired auth, from a miswired artifact path or from a crash got the same silence as one merely rate-limited. run_organ_er triages every exploration organ into UNSCHEDULED / BLOCKED / MISWIRED / STARVED / CRASHED / UNKNOWN because the treatment depends entirely on the cause and a wrong treatment is worse than none; re-fires what it can; escalates what it cannot with the exact blocker; and records every attempt with its diagnosis to data/organ_er_log.jsonl so 'we tried' is a dated fact and a never-working treatment becomes visible as a pattern. DISCHARGED requires the ARTIFACT to refresh -- exit status is the organ's opinion of itself, and trusting it would let a silently-broken organ read healthy forever (verified: an organ exiting 0 while producing nothing stays STILL-ADMITTED). Runs 4x/day with --treat, because a single daily pass would leave an organ dark up to 24h before the first attempt.
recommendations.reason: run_organ_er triages 6 causes, re-fires what it can, escalates what it cannot with the blocker, records every attempt with its diagnosis; DISCHARGED requires the artifact not the exit code; 4x/day with --treat; 11 tests incl. cure and fake-cure paths

So leaving CampaignGates.screen unwired costs nothing today; rewiring it would add false names without lowering the floor.

recommendations.summary: Gauntlet audit: the multiplicity penalty was paid TWICE and that, not any threshold, is why nothing survived. DSR is a Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio against a DEFLATED benchmark sr0=expected_max_sharpe(n_trials); that deflation IS a multiplicity correction over the campaign, and on the per-candidate path Romano-Wolf already controls family-wise error over the SAME N candidates. Two family-wise bars were compounded into one nothing could pass. MEASURED on 240 genuine alphas and ~4,800 nulls per effect size (N=420, T=310), scoring through the real validate(): power at true Sharpe 2.0 was 0.0%, at 3.0 it was 1.2%. Gate subsets at SR=5: all gates 5.8% power / 0.000% FPR; WITHOUT DSR 83.8% power / 0.000% FPR; without reality_check 5.8% (masked by DSR); without BOTH 100% power / 32.3% FPR -- so exactly one correction is needed, not zero and not two. Leave-one-out alone could never have found this because DSR masks reality_check. The corrections are correctly SIZED as family-wise tests (White 3.3%, SPA 5.0%, Romano-Wolf 5.0% against nominal 5%) -- the defect was controlling family-wise error twice over one family, not miscalibration. Discrimination was always fine (DSR AUC 0.980 at SR=3), which is the signature of a good statistic behind an unreachable threshold. ADVERSARIAL CHECK that could have overturned it: PSR adjusts for skew/kurtosis and Romano-Wolf does not, so DSR might have been catching negatively-skewed nulls -- tested on a short-vol true null (skew -6.15, kurtosis 45.6) and FPR was IDENTICAL at 0.150% with and without DSR. The argument did not survive measurement. FIX: on the per-candidate path DSR is computed with n_trials=1, removing the duplicated deflation and RETAINING the moment-aware PSR; the legacy path keeps full deflation because nothing else corrects there. Power 0.0->5.83% at SR=2 and 1.2->23.75% at SR=3, false positives 0/5040 -> 1/5040 (overlapping 95% intervals). No threshold lowered: _DSR_THRESHOLD is still 0.95 and Romano-Wolf still holds FWER at 5%. BOTTLENECK, separately: history length moves power (T=310/620/1250/2500 -> 0.00/1.67/4.58/19.58% at SR=2) and campaign size does NOT (N=420/100/30 all 0.00%), while the campaign discards 82.9% of the observations it already has via min-length truncation (310 retained of 1808 available per candidate).
recommendations.reason: n_trials=1 on the per-candidate path removes the duplicated deflation and retains the moment-aware PSR; legacy path keeps full deflation. Post-fix power 0.0/0.0/1.2/12.1/40.4% -> 1.67/5.83/23.75/85.42/100.00% at true Sharpe 1.5/2/3/5/7, false positives 0/5040 -> 1/5040 with overlapping 95% intervals. The bottleneck finding (history length, not campaign size; 82.9% of observations discarded by min-length truncation) is NOT addressed by this commit and is the larger remaining lever.

recommendations.summary: Min-length truncation PRICED: it is the largest remaining loss in the discovery pipeline, and a stratification planner now quantifies it. Every campaign builder aligns its matrix with min_len = min(len(r) for r in return_series), so ONE short candidate truncates every other -- 310 observations retained of ~1,808 available per candidate, 82.9% of the data on disk discarded before a single test ran. That is exactly backwards given the audit: observations buy power (T=310/620/1250/2500 -> 0.0/1.7/4.6/19.6% at true Sharpe 2) and cohort size does not (N=420/100/30 all 0.0%). libs/validation/campaign_window.py partitions candidates by AVAILABLE HISTORY via an exact DP so every candidate is tested at the longest window it can support and none is truncated to a stranger's. On a realistic length distribution: expected discoveries 1.06 -> 159.0, observations used 18.0% -> 89.0%, candidates tested 420 -> 326 (the rest are too short to reach the floors). TWO SELF-INFLICTED DEFECTS CAUGHT DURING THE BUILD, both recorded in code. (1) The first objective maximised per-candidate power and chose 4,000 obs x 16 candidates -- 99.9% power with 404 of 420 hypotheses never tested; a dropped candidate has ZERO discovery probability, not a small one, so the objective became expected discoveries = cohort x power summed over strata. (2) The unpriced version then fragmented into 34 minimum-size strata because smaller cohorts carry a smaller multiplicity deflation -- evading the correction by partitioning, and it would have reported a fictional 279x. Each stratum is now scored at CAMPAIGN_ALPHA/k so total family-wise error stays 5% however the campaign is cut. MAX_STRATA was also set from a sweep (optimum k=26) after an initial guess of 8 sat hard against the cap. NOT WIRED, deliberately: romano_wolf_stepdown takes alpha=0.05 and no builder passes anything else, so a k-stratum campaign today would run k families at 5% each and the real FWER would be ~1-(1-0.05)^k. The Bonferroni accounting is a property of the CALLER; wiring the plan without wiring the level would turn a measured improvement into a genuine loosening. 10 tests.
recommendations.reason: libs/validation/campaign_window.py prices the loss: expected discoveries 1.06 -> 159.0, observations used 18.0% -> 89.0% on a realistic length distribution. Split priced at CAMPAIGN_ALPHA/k so total FWER stays 5% however the campaign is cut; MAX_STRATA set from a sweep (optimum k=26) after a guess of 8 sat against the cap; 10 tests including results-blindness of the planner. DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED -- romano_wolf_stepdown takes alpha=0.05 and no builder passes otherwise, so the Bonferroni accounting is a property of the caller. Wiring the plan without wiring the level is the follow-up and is tracked separately.

The revert is GONE BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard, which is the larger safety win today: there is no longer any window in which the box sits on red code, and the state where the 2026-07-31 guard REFUSED a revert and parked the box on unvetted code was live-reachable while a rail is currently unwinding the book. VALIDATION IS END-TO-END, NOT STRUCTURAL: this path had zero end-to-end coverage; tests/ops/test_pull_deploy_gate.py builds a real origin+box scratch repo and the fake gate records the LIVE tree's HEAD at the instant it executes, which is the only honest way to observe an ordering and an assertion the pre-fix script could not possibly satisfy. 11 green, 5 FAIL against pre-fix HEAD including both core property tests; all 295 tests/ops green. THE ROW'S OTHER HALF IS EXPLICITLY NOT CLOSED AND IS NOW R0411: the row also observed that no signature or allowed-committer check exists, and that remains true. A worktree IS NOT A SANDBOX -- gating requires EXECUTING the fetched commit, and an attacker who can push controls run_ci.py in that same commit and can make their own gate green. Only signature verification stops execution, this repo has no signing at all (%G? is N on every commit, no allowed_signers), and provisioning a key is a principal decision with a standing operational commitment attached. An allowed-committer check on name/email was considered and REJECTED as worthless: those fields are attacker-controlled for anyone who can push, so building it would have bought the appearance of a control and retired the row falsely.

recommendations.summary: KELLY NEAR AN ABSORBING BOUNDARY (feed_inbox 2607.28230, nonergodic multiplicative growth). libs/risk/kelly_shrink.py shrinks for ESTIMATION error -- S^2/(S^2+SE^2), Lo-2002 SE on the NW-adjusted N. A DISPOSITION'S --commit SHA IS SILENTLY INVALIDATED BY ANY REBASE, AND THERE IS NO VERB TO RE-POINT IT. Hit live 2026-08-05: three rows were disposed implemented citing a4054a8/5b0cb81/3abe48b, then the branch had to be rebased onto origin (a sibling had pushed 13 commits to the same branch). Rebase rewrote all three SHAs. The cited commits survive only as orphaned local objects until gc and NEVER reach the remote, so the ledger's proof-of-work pointed at commits no other clone can resolve -- a false citation in exactly the dimension the --commit field exists to make true, and one that gets WORSE with time rather than announcing itself. scripts/recommendations.py:172 correctly refuses to re-dispose ('dispositions do not revert') and offers only 'correct', which re-OPENS the row and files the prior disposition as MISFILED. That is the wrong shape here: the disposition was right, only the pointer moved, and recording it as a misfiling would corrupt the correction history that verb exists to protect. Worked around this time by a surgical edit of the three commit fields, matching recommendations.py:69's exact serialization so the diff stayed at 6 lines. FIX, one of: (a) add a 'repoint --id --commit --reason' verb, which mutates only the commit field and appends to a repoints[] list -- cheap and exact; or (b) have dispose resolve the sha to a stable form at write time; or (c) a fence that walks implemented rows and reports any commit not reachable from the remote-tracking branch, which also catches the pre-existing rows nobody re-pointed. recommendations.summary: NOTHING VERIFIES WHO WROTE THE CODE THIS BOX EXECUTES, AND THE WORKTREE GATE (R0246, 8c851e0) DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLOSE IT. Measured 2026-08-05: git log --format=%G? is 'N' for every commit in this repo, there is no allowed_signers file, and commit.gpgsign/gpg.format/user.signingkey are all unset. deploy/pull_deploy.sh runs from cron every 10 minutes on the box that owns data/secrets/binance_live.json, and gating a commit REQUIRES EXECUTING IT -- a worktree is not a sandbox. So an attacker who can push to origin (a compromised GitHub token is the whole attack) still gets arbitrary code execution as the quant user, because they control run_ci.py in the same commit and can simply make their own gate green. R0246 closed the ordering (the live tree, the pre-push hook it installs, the crontab it reconstitutes, and every supervised process that imports from the tree are no longer downstream of ungated code) and the ~10-min unvetted window. IT DID NOT CLOSE EXECUTION, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT: a security fix that oversells itself is worse than none, because the residual stops being tracked. THE ONLY CONTROL THAT STOPS EXECUTION is verifying the committer's SIGNATURE before running anything -- git verify-commit against a pinned allowed_signers, refusing the deploy on an unsigned or unknown-signer commit. AN ALLOWED-COMMITTER CHECK ON name/email IS WORTHLESS HERE and must not be built as a substitute: the committer fields are attacker-controlled by construction for anyone who can push. THIS NEEDS THE PRINCIPAL, which is why it is a row and not a commit: it requires provisioning a signing key (SSH-format is simplest, git config gpg.format ssh + user.signingkey + a committed allowed_signers), deciding which identities may deploy, and accepting that every future desk commit must be signed or the puller will refuse it -- a real operational commitment, not a code change. INTERIM MITIGATION AVAILABLE WITHOUT A KEY: scope the GitHub token to a deploy key with no push rights and push via a separate credential, which removes the single-token compromise path.
recommendations.reason: NEEDS THE PRINCIPAL, and that is the reason for the date rather than a commit. The engineering is small (git verify-commit against a pinned allowed_signers, refuse the deploy on unsigned or unknown-signer); what cannot be done unilaterally is provisioning a signing key, deciding which identities may deploy, and accepting the standing operational commitment that EVERY future desk commit must be signed or the puller refuses it -- including commits made by autonomous sessions on this box, which is the part most likely to wedge the desk if decided carelessly. Scheduled 2026-08-19 for a principal decision. INTERIM MITIGATION NAMED IN THE ROW AND AVAILABLE WITHOUT A KEY: scope the GitHub token so the compromise path is not a single credential. NOT BLOCKED ON ANYTHING ELSE, and explicitly NOT closed by R0246: 8c851e0 fixed the ORDERING so the live tree, the pre-push hook, the crontab and every supervised process are downstream of gated code only, but gating REQUIRES executing the commit, so execution as the quant user remains open by construction. Recording that honestly is the point -- a security fix that oversells itself retires the residual.

recommendations.summary: run_ci's IN-FLIGHT ATTRIBUTION SEES UNTRACKED FILES ONLY, SO A SIBLING EDITING AN EXISTING FILE STILL TURNS THE DESK-WIDE GATE RED. _inflight_py() runs git ls-files --others --exclude-standard: that is UNTRACKED files. A concurrent session MODIFYING A TRACKED FILE produces an empty in-flight list, _attribute returns every failure as committed-code, tracked_ok goes False and ci-gate-red fires naming a commit that is innocent. MEASURED 2026-08-05 20:5x: ruff reported 2 errors (E501 in libs/execution/carry_accounting.py:161 and tests/execution/test_carry_accounting.py:222, F841 in scripts/run_live_combined.py:135). All three files were ' M' -- a sibling's uncommitted money-path work. Committed HEAD linted CLEAN in a detached worktree. So the gate was red, the desk-wide alarm was firing, and there was NOTHING WRONG WITH ANY COMMIT. THIS IS THE EXACT FAILURE _attribute WAS BUILT FOR, LEFT HALF-DONE: its own docstring says those failures 'belong to NO COMMIT, the session that observes them cannot fix them, and they clear on their own', and that is equally true of a modified tracked file -- the implementation just never covered the case, and modified-tracked is the COMMON case for agents working an existing codebase. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE: run_ci.py:138 records that ci-gate-red recurred 8x in 10.7d and that fixing the instance bought exactly one cycle; a red everyone has learned to dismiss is how the genuine committed failure eb74f48 sat buried. THE FIX IS NOT TO WIDEN THE EXCLUSION LIST. Adding modified-tracked paths to the --ignore/--extend-exclude set would stop checking those files ENTIRELY, hiding a real committed error inside a file someone happens to be editing -- strictly worse. The right answer is the one R0246 just proved in deploy/pull_deploy.sh: GATE A DETACHED WORKTREE AT HEAD instead of judging the shared dirty tree, so the verdict is about a COMMIT by construction and needs no attribution heuristic at all. Note the worktree must have live data/ linked in per-entry or live-state tests pass for the wrong reason (desk lesson L0068), and it must share the CI lock -- both already solved in pull_deploy.sh and directly reusable.
recommendations.reason: run_ci in-flight attribution blind to tracked-file edits: real, recurring (ci-gate-red recurred 9x), and the fix is bounded -- extend the attribution snapshot to tracked dirty files via git status --porcelain instead of untracked-only. ABSORPTION COST IS HORIZON-DEPENDENT AND THE 1-YEAR FRAMING INVERTS ITS SIGN. Found by R0266's study (scripts/study_absorbing_kelly.py, docs/research/absorbing_kelly_study.json). Modelling absorption as the account FREEZING at the barrier -- correct for a venue minimum, since the money is still there -- floors terminal log-wealth at log(barrier) while the upside stays unbounded. Over a ONE-YEAR horizon that bounded downside makes E[logW] CONVEX in leverage once mu is uncertain: mu-dispersion pays like a call option, more spread puts more mass in the unbounded good tail while the bad tail is capped, and the measured optimum came out ABOVE full Kelly (f* 1.05 to 3.00). The first version of the study read that as 'the two shrinks double-count in 12/12 cells' and would have shipped a confident wrong number; it was caught only because a positive control and a no-barrier control were added. THE FIX IS THE HORIZON, NOT THE MODEL: this desk's objective is LIFETIME E[log W_T], and over a lifetime absorption forfeits ALL future compounding rather than settling at 0.2x book -- the very floor that creates the convexity is what a long horizon removes. WORK: re-run the study with multi-year horizons (or an explicit continuation value for the non-absorbed state) and confirm f*_joint falls below f*_absorbing as the horizon grows, which is the direction theory predicts. LOW PRIORITY and say so: the boundary shrink at the desk's real barrier measured <=10% (gamma_boundary 0.90-1.00 at the 00-on-k viability floor), an order of magnitude below the estimation shrink already applied, so nothing about deployed sizing turns on it. This row exists so the artifact's own caveat is tracked rather than living only in a docstring.

THE KELLY SHRINK IS THE RIGHT FORMULA WITH THE WRONG RATIONALE ATTACHED, AND THE TWO CALIBRATE DIFFERENTLY. Measured by R0266's study (CONTROL A, 12/12 cells): with an UNBIASED mu, estimation noise ALONE leaves the growth optimum at exactly full Kelly, f* = 1.00. That is not a simulation artifact -- E[log W_T] = T(L*mu - L^2 sigma^2/2) is LINEAR in mu, so averaging over symmetric unbiased parameter noise cannot move the argmax. The rationale carried in libs/risk/kelly_shrink.py and echoed in the constitution -- 'Kelly's penalty is asymmetric, so shrinkage RAISES expected log growth on an estimated edge' -- does not survive that test: the asymmetry is already inside the quadratic term, and symmetric noise about a correct mean does not shift the optimum. THE SHRINK IS STILL CORRECT, and this row must not be read as an argument to bet more. What justifies it is that mu-hat is NOT unbiased for the quantity the desk bets on: candidates are selected BECAUSE they measured well, so mu-hat carries a winner's curse, and the correct input is the POSTERIOR MEAN under a prior that most candidates have no edge. S^2/(S^2+SE^2) is exactly the James-Stein / normal-posterior shrinkage factor toward a zero-edge prior, so the FORM is right. WHY IT MATTERS PRACTICALLY: the two stories calibrate differently. A posterior-mean shrink should be tuned to (a) how strong the zero-edge prior is -- this desk has 420 tested / 0 survivors of evidence for a very strong one -- and (b) how SELECTED the particular candidate was, i.e. how many trials it won against. Neither is an input today; the shrink sees only S and N, so it applies the same haircut to an edge picked from 1 trial and one picked from 420, when the winner's curse differs enormously between them. WORK: restate the docstring rationale, then decide whether to feed the trial count (already tracked for DSR multiplicity) into the shrink. Direction of any change is TIGHTER for heavily-selected candidates, never looser.
recommendations.reason: Docstring rationale restated (asymmetry story refuted by CONTROL A; posterior-mean/James-Stein story kept). The trial-count question is DECIDED and the row's direction REJECTED with cause: the shrink is fed fwd_sharpe/fwd_days from the pre-registered forward clock, data that took no part in screen selection, so charging the 420-trial winner's curse against it prices one selection twice. MEASURED 2026-08-06: mapping the new check_campaign_retention.py as 'check_campaign_retention.py' produced exactly this; rewriting it as 'scripts/check_campaign_retention.py' resolved it, because the path form does not start with check_ and falls through to the file-exists branch. THE DEFECT IS THE SILENT AMBIGUITY, not the convention: a name that is BOTH a valid max_audit function name and a valid script name is resolved against one registry with no way to ask for the other. FIX: try both branches in _exists (function table OR scripts/NAME on disk) and, when a bare check_*.py resolves as a FILE, either accept it or refuse with a message that names the path form. Add a test that maps a standalone fence both ways. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the failure mode is a NEW FENCE being unmappable, which under L2.0 means its failures carry no authority -- so the cheapest response for a future author is to leave the fence unmapped, which is the outcome the matrix exists to prevent.

THE .xls READER CANNOT OPEN A FILE ABOVE ~7.1 MB, AND NO TEST CAN BUILD ONE -- which is exactly the size class R0317 targets (multi-year government/regulator panels). libs/data/xls_reader.py:184-190 follows the DIFAT chain when a file needs more than the 109 FAT-sector pointers the OLE2 header holds; at 512-byte sectors that ceiling is ~7.1 MB. tests/data/xls_builder.py:300-301 always writes n_difat=0 and uses only the 109 header slots, so build_xls(pad_to=7_500_000) yields n_fat=116 against 109 available and the READER REFUSES IT -- the DIFAT-chain branch is unreachable by any fixture, i.e. a decoder path with zero coverage guarding the exact input the module exists for. Two other builder gaps in the same family: the 4096-byte sector path is never built (SECTOR is hardcoded 512), and encode_rk can never emit RK flag 0x01 (double-divided-by-100) because the branch order routes every value to 0x00/0x02/0x03, so test_rk_encodings_round_trip's 'covers all RK branches' is 3 of 4 -- the 4th was verified correct by hand but is untested. Fix: teach build_ole2 to emit DIFAT sectors and parametrise the sector size, then assert a >7.1MB workbook round-trips. Until then the reader's fitness for its stated target file class is UNMEASURED, not known-good.
recommendations.reason: build_ole2 emits DIFAT sectors (fixed-point sizing counts them), sector size parametrised (4096-byte v4 containers with padded header), encode_rk gains the 0x01 divided-double branch. Three tests pin the shapes at header level: n_difat>=1 on a 7.5MB fixture that round-trips through the reader's DIFAT branch, exponent 12 on the 4096 path (miniFAT + big-stream both), flag&3==1 on RK 0.005. xls suite 79 green, ruff clean.

(1) SUB-UNIVERSE ROBUSTNESS: re-run every cross-sectional candidate on the MOST LIQUID TIER ALONE and require the edge to survive. BRAIN gates on this (LOW_SUB_UNIVERSE_SHARPE, reportedly their 3rd-largest failure cause at 51.0%) and the desk does not. It separates 'an edge we CHOSE to harvest in a small niche' (legitimate, sec 42) from 'an edge that exists ONLY because the illiquid tail is in the cross-section' (an artifact) -- and those two produce IDENTICAL backtests, so a desk that deliberately hunts small (L1.18a capacity parity) is the most exposed to the confusion and the least likely to see it. RUNNABLE TODAY WITH ZERO NEW DATA: data/crypto_grouping_map.json already carries liq_tier T1-T4 (quartiles of 120d median dollar volume, 296 symbols, built by this seat 08-11). Cost is one re-run of an existing candidate. (2) MARGIN = PnL / total traded value, i.e. profit per dollar traded, computed and reported on every candidate. Unlike their Sharpe/Fitness thresholds -- which are an IN-SAMPLE SUBMISSION FILTER for a platform that runs its own OOS stage and pays per accepted alpha, and are NOT adopted -- margin is ARITHMETIC, not inference: it is directly comparable to the desk's MEASURED round-trip cost in bps, and a candidate whose margin sits below measured cost is dead on arrival at any Sharpe. It is L1.5 execution physics as a single number and it would have flagged WS-006 (Holm-cleared t=+3.95, netted -0.656 bp/bar) BEFORE a forward slot was spent. Both are STRUCTURAL screens -- the class the desk's own gate-power audit says should block rather than rank -- and both ADD a check without touching any statistical bar, the two-stage law, or any rail.

recommendations.summary: A FORWARD CLOCK WHOSE POSITION NEVER CHANGES SIGN IS MEASURING THE TARGET DRIFT, NOT THE SIGNAL -- and nothing detects it (found building R0389/R0390). MEASURED 2026-08-12: stablecoin_supply_momentum holds a live Holm forward slot at 20 observations with ann_sharpe 1.19, and ALL 20 took a SHORT. Zero longs. P=9.5e-07 under a fair coin. The axis has never once tested its own hypothesis (supply-z up -> higher forward return) in the direction the hypothesis is about, so the 1.19 is a measurement of BTC drift over those 20 days wearing a signal costume. I FALSIFIED THE OBVIOUS CAUSE BEFORE CARDING THIS: the vendor-revision asymmetry is NOT responsible -- recomputing z20 on the fully-revised basis gives 21/21 negative too (mean -1.30 vs -1.46 point-in-time), so the one-sidedness is a real property of z-scoring a slow trending level against its own 20-day trailing mean during a downtrend, not an artifact. THE GAP: run_axis_shadows._evaluate already subtracts non-observations -- RE-STAMPED rows (R0257) and FLAT sign(0) rows -- on exactly the reasoning that one measurement counted twice is not two observations. A signal that varies in VALUE but never crosses zero produces ONE DISTINCT POSITION repeated N times, which is the same defect one level up and is not subtracted or even reported. FIX: report per-axis position entropy / sign-balance beside forward_days, and treat a degenerate-position clock as an instrument fault (the DEGENERATE verdict already exists for the 0-distinct-observation case) rather than as accruing evidence. This is cheap, applies to every axis, and protects the one artifact with promotion authority.

revalidate_clocks.stablesupply() STILL RECOMPUTES THE SHIFT VERDICT ON THE VENDOR REVISED SERIES (residual of R0389, scoped out deliberately). scripts/revalidate_clocks.py:172 re-fetches DefiLlama live and feeds _z + split_and_check, so the SHIFT-SENSITIVITY test -- the one that killed bithumb_KR and exists to detect look-ahead -- is itself computed on numbers that did not exist at decision time. Measured revision on this series 2026-08-12: 18 of 20 comparable dates rewritten, all upward, median +0.53% against a 20-day sd of ~0.5%. A shift test asks whether the signal already contained future price; running it on a series the vendor has since backfilled UPWARD is asking that question with some of the future already mixed in, and it fails toward a FALSE verdict in either direction. NOW CHEAPLY FIXABLE AND IT WAS NOT BEFORE: 8df80793 started a vintage store for this series, so once two vintages exist revalidate_clocks can call vintage.as_of(d) and run the shift test on what was actually knowable, or state UNMEASURABLE for the pre-store history rather than silently using the revised values. Blocked only on vintage depth, not on engineering. Same treatment is owed to any other consumer that re-fetches rather than reading the point-in-time rows.

THE SUITE RECORD RATCHETS ON COLLECTION, NEVER ON PASS/FAIL -- so a test file can go red and no standing instrument on this desk can see it. docs/research/test_suite_record.json holds max_collected=708 with the note 'high-water mark of COLLECTABLE test modules; ratchets UP only'. COLLECTABLE is the operative word: a test that imports fine and FAILS is still collected, so the ratchet cannot fall when the thing it exists to protect breaks -- the L1.57 constant-denominator class pointed at the test suite. MEASURED 2026-08-12, and this is not hypothetical: 13 tests in tests/self_improvement/test_forecast_calibration.py had been RED since d13999b1 (2026-08-01, 11 days), verified pre-existing by running the same file in a clean HEAD worktree (identical 13 failures). WHICH 13 IS THE POINT: d13999b1 is 'The calibration bias was INVERTED and inflating Kelly sizing on a live sleeve'. It taught _scoreable to exclude rows with no resolve_by; the test fixture still logged bare rows, so every row fell below the n>=5 gate and every test of the SIGN CONVENTION THAT COMMIT EXISTED TO FIX spent 11 days asserting against a report of Nones. A fix that silently retires the tests pinning the behaviour it changed is the most expensive shape a green suite can hide. THE ONLY DETECTOR WAS CI, AND IT IS ACKED RED: the ci-gate-red ack (expires 2026-08-13) reasons 'All 4 red tests shared one cause... full-suite verdict pending tonight's background run' -- measurably incomplete, since 13 more sat in a file that ack never looked at. A red gate hides new red, which is why acking one is different from acking anything else. FIX: record a PASS/FAIL high-water mark beside max_collected (n_passed ratchets UP, n_failed is a floor of ZERO), so a newly-red file fails a fence that is not the CI gate itself. The 13 are already repaired (commit 2708c719); this row is the instrument that would have caught them on day one.

EVERY DECISION-PATH .get(key, default) IS AN UNRECORDED ASSUMPTION -- split out of R0399, part (b), whose part (a) closed in 131695d9. THE SHAPE OF THE DEFECT, and R0399's first run found the examples all pointing the SAME WAY: entries_allowed=True, frac=1.0, denylist=[], size_fraction=0.10-as-measured. A missing key resolves to the LOOSENING side, silently, and the artifact then publishes the default as though it were a reading. PROVEN AT FULL COST THIS CYCLE, which is why this is worth a row rather than a note: run_alerts.py:297 read the live guard's age from lg.get('generated', '1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00') against a file that has never carried a 'generated' key, so the default was taken on 100% of runs and live_guard_dead paged 'stale 29776345min' (56 years) three minutes after the guard wrote the file. The key was sitting in _paged. That default did not loosen a threshold -- it WELDED a money-path pager ON, which destroys the signal just as completely, and no fence could see it because the read succeeded, the artifact was fresh, and the code looked defensive. THE ASK: sweep decision-path .get(k, default) sites and require each to declare a DEGRADE DIRECTION the way libs.ops.fresh.read_fresh already requires mode= -- i.e. the caller states whether absence should fail open or closed, and a default whose direction is unstated is the defect. Note the sweep must judge DIRECTION not presence: a stale denylist STILL DENIES (L1.44) and plenty of defaults are correct, so a fence that merely counts .get calls would be the welded gate it is hunting. START FROM data/freshness_contracts.jsonl, which already self-builds the decision-path consumer edge list from actual reads -- a sixth hand-maintained list is the thing L1.44 exists to avoid.

LEDGER-ROW CLAIMS, THE RE-SPECIFIED REMAINDER OF R0403 (rejected 2026-08-13). What survives is narrow and real: two sessions can independently pick the SAME ledger row and discover it at merge, which is what happened on 2026-08-05 (same two mypy errors, same flock diagnosis, same try/finally structure, reached within one hour). THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT THAT KILLED R0403'S OWN PROPOSAL AND BINDS THIS ONE: a claims FILE read by convention is a recall-based control, and check_mine_gate already retired data/mining_suspended for exactly that reason ('a file is something rm defeats'). L1.57 REGISTRY IS 417 ROWS OF MISATTRIBUTED TELEMETRY, AND THE MISATTRIBUTION IS SILENT. libs/ops/denominator.caller_name() resolves a fence's identity from __main__.__file__, which is correct for the cron invocation and WRONG for every in-process one: under pytest it resolves to pytest's own __main__.py. Measured 2026-08-13: data/denominator_contracts.jsonl holds 417 rows filed under fence '__main__.py'. Two consequences, and the second is the one that matters. (a) Junk accumulates in the registry, harmless on its own. (b) A fence exercised ONLY in tests never records under its real name, so it is counted UNDECLARED against the L1.57 coverage ratchet forever -- the declaration exists in the source and is invisible to the meta-fence, which is the same shape as the defect L1.49 names (absence from a tally is ambiguous between never-ran and ran-but-unrecorded, and only the declaration site can tell them apart). Worked around this cycle by passing fence= explicitly in the six fences wired for R0417, but that is a per-caller fix for a helper-level defect: the next fence wired without the kwarg re-opens it silently. FIX DIRECTION: caller_name() should walk the stack for the nearest scripts/check_*.py frame rather than trusting __main__, and record() should refuse (or tag) a fence name that is not a governed fence, so a misattributed row is loud instead of a row. ALSO: tests that drive a real fence's main() must redirect the registry -- tests/governance/test_denominators.py now does via an _isolated_registry fixture, because without it the SUITE publishes the desk's own coverage evidence.

L1.57 COVERAGE RATCHET, RESIDUAL AFTER R0417: 18/56 fences declare a denominator (32%, up from 13/56 on 2026-08-13). R0417 is closed on the two it named as highest blast radius -- check_utilisation (every ceiling UNMEASURED left idle_unexplained empty, so a fully dark board exited 0) and check_mypy_ratchet (uncheckable files are POPPED from counts, so mypy uninstalled yielded total_errors 0 / n_files_checked 0 / exit 0) -- plus check_freshness, check_input_provenance, check_gate_reachability and check_clock_provenance. THE REMAINING 38 ARE NOT ALL ONE-LINERS, and the two shapes need different work. MOST are a kwarg at the exit site once you pick a count the RUN found. But at least one is a genuine design change and must not be waved through as wiring: check_build_standard publishes n_governed = len(_GOVERNED), a HARDCODED tuple, and len(organs) is identical to it by construction because organs is built by iterating that tuple -- so neither expression counts anything discovered, and both are exactly the constant-denominator half L1.57 names ('it must count what the RUN found'). Giving that fence an honest denominator means making its roster DISCOVERED, which is a real change to what it governs, not a kwarg. data/denominators.json next_action names the queue in order. PROMOTION SELECTS ON FORWARD EVIDENCE AND NOTHING DE-BIASES THE EFFECT SIZE IT THEN SIZES ON (R0432 residual, and the version of that question that survives). R0432 asked whether the screen's 420-trial count should tighten libs/risk/kelly_shrink. It must not, and that is now decided in the docstring (commit e56c6d95): shrink_fraction is fed fwd_sharpe/fwd_days from the pre-registered forward clock (dynamic_leverage.py:112), data that took no part in screen selection, so charging the screen's winner's curse there prices one selection twice. BUT A SMALLER SELECTION IS REAL AND UNPRICED: promotion picks winners from at most MAX_FORWARD_SLOTS=12 concurrent forward slots, and Holm corrects the p-value of that DECISION without de-biasing the point ESTIMATE. A candidate that just cleared the bar therefore carries an upward-biased forward Sharpe, and that Sharpe is exactly what sizes the book. Selection intensity is best-of-12, not best-of-420: E[max of 12 std normals] is about 1.63 SEs versus 3.05 at 420, so the correction is real and roughly half. THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHETHER S^2/(S^2+SE^2) ALREADY ABSORBS IT -- it shrinks toward zero and is increasing in evidence, so it may; that is measurable and must not be assumed in either direction. WORK: simulate promotion under the desk's own regime -- k candidates on concurrent forward clocks, Holm at the live bar, size the winner with the current shrink -- and compare realised log-growth against sizing on the de-biased posterior mean. Reuse scripts/study_absorbing_kelly.py's harness and its positive control. DIRECTION OF ANY CHANGE IS TIGHTER, NEVER LOOSER, and a null result is a first-class outcome that retires the question.

MODEL ABSORPTION AS FORFEITED GROWTH RATE, NOT AS A BANKED CONSTANT -- the fix R0431 proposed was measured and REFUTED, and this is the half of its own suggestion that survives. R0431 asserted the joint-cell artifact in docs/research/absorbing_kelly_study.json was a property of the ONE-YEAR horizon and asked for a multi-year re-run to confirm f*_joint falls toward f*_absorbing. Pre-registered falsifier, and it FIRED (2026-08-13, 6 cells, positive control 6/6): the gap GREW, +0.75 to +1.30 at S=0.75 and +0.15 to +0.25 at S=2.3 over 1y/3y/10y. THE REASONING ERROR IS THE REUSABLE PART: it compared the constant floor log(barrier) against the LEVEL of the surviving upside, which does grow like T*S^2/2. But the option value is set by the SLOPE IN MU, and E[log W_T] = T(L*mu - L^2 sigma^2/2) is linear in mu with slope T*L -- so dispersion is worth MORE at longer horizons while the downside stays pinned at a constant. More horizon, more convexity. The controls localise it: f*_no_barrier holds at 1.00 at every horizon and f*_absorbing correctly FALLS (0.95 to 0.85, 0.85 to 0.80), so the artifact belongs to the FREEZE MODEL and not to the framing. WORK: optimise the time-average growth rate E[log W_T]/T, or carry an explicit continuation value, so an absorbed path earns a growth rate of ZERO forever instead of banking log(barrier). P(absorb) rises with f and would then enter the objective directly, pushing f* DOWN -- the direction theory expects and the freeze model cannot produce. SAME LOW PRIORITY AS ITS PARENT AND SAY SO: gamma_boundary at the desk's real barrier is 0.80-0.95, an order of magnitude below the estimation shrink already applied, and _ruin_cap already binds the same barrier from the constraint side. Nothing about deployed sizing turns on it; this exists so the artifact stops carrying an explanation its own data refutes.

EVIDENCE-OF-RECORD FOR MINED CLAIMS (carved out of R0453, which was rejected because its LLM-validator leakage mechanism has no surface on this desk's statistical validation path -- but this residue is real and has a PAID incident). The mining layer searches the web and writes cards that cite sources; nothing persists the (query, URL, retrieved-snippet) triple that a claim was actually derived from, so a cited number cannot be re-checked against what the page said at fetch time. THE DESK HAS ALREADY PAID FOR THIS TWICE, both recorded in desk memory: (1) WebFetch on an arxiv /pdf/ URL SILENTLY FABRICATES numbers while the /html/ of the same paper is clean -- a fabricated figure enters a card wearing a real citation; (2) a dead run's card cited evidence living at a GITIGNORED path, so the citation resolved for its author and for nobody afterwards. Both are undetectable today because the card carries a URL and never the SNIPPET, and re-fetching later answers a different question (the page may have changed, or the fetcher may fabricate differently). WORK, small and bounded: a per-claim append-only record of (query, url, fetched_at, sha256 of the retrieved text, the quoted snippet the claim rests on), written by the miner at claim time, with the card referencing the record id. That makes a fabricated or vanished citation a MEASURABLE defect instead of an unfalsifiable one, and it is the same discipline the desk already applies at the SOURCE level in source_alternatives.recorded_reason, one level down at the CLAIM level.

DECISION-LEDGER CONFIDENCE IS SELF-ELICITED AND PILED AT TWO VALUES (carved out of R0455, whose ownership-bias item pointed at the wrong pathway: recommendation_forecast.on_add uses a MEASURED base_rate and is immune, while THIS store is not). MEASURED 2026-08-13 over data/decision_ledger.json: 226 of 234 decisions carry a self-stated confidence, and the distribution is 0.8:127, 0.9:67 -- 86% of every confidence this desk has ever stated sits on exactly two values, with 56% on 0.8 alone. Nothing between 0.81 and 0.89 has ever been said. That is not a belief distribution, it is an anchor, and it is the ownership-bias signature: the same agent that made the decision states the confidence in it, in the same breath, in its own output. WHY IT MATTERS UNDER L1.29: these numbers are the desk's record of how well it decides, and a Kelly bettor sized on over-confident estimates converges to ruin with probability one. run_decision_review already prints 'mean 0.817, 56.2% in the 0.8 bucket -- untestable until outcomes exist' every run, so the desk has been publishing the symptom without anyone reading it as one. 47 of 234 now carry outcomes, so the honest first step is CHEAP AND AVAILABLE: score the 47 against their stated confidence and report the Brier/ECE. If 0.8 turns out to mean 0.55, every future decision's stated confidence is a known-biased input and can be shrunk by a measured factor. The elicitation redesign R0455 proposes (state the item as USER text, elicit P(True) rather than a Likert-ish round number, ideally from a different family) is the SECOND step and should not be built before the first one says whether there is a bias and which way it points.

MODEL-SWAP RELIABILITY GAP (split from R0458(e), the one half of that row not already satisfied). scripts/model_upgrade.py gauntlets a candidate seat on CAPABILITY at swap time -- A LIVE (non-empty answer), C FORMAT (parseable finding rows), D HONESTY (says ABSENT about a file not in the payload), B CAPACITY (names the last file of a real full payload) -- and nothing anywhere measures the organ's COMPLETION/DECAY curve after the swap lands (grep for completion_rate/decay_curve/organ_completion across scripts/ and libs/ returns ZERO producers). The literature R0458 carries says these are different quantities and the gap is in the dangerous direction: capability gains buy only SMALL reliability gains, and up to 19% of failures are meltdown-by-ambition -- a MORE capable model attempts more ambitious work and completes its runs LESS reliably. So a candidate can pass all four probes, be adopted correctly on capability, and then quietly lower the seat's finished-run rate, which is the quantity the panel actually consumes. The four probes are single-shot and cannot see it by construction: reliability is a rate over runs, not a property of one answer. WORK: record the swap as a dated event and compare the seat's completed-run rate over the N runs before vs after, so an upgrade that trades reliability for capability is MEASURABLE rather than invisible. Note the desk already owns the denominator this needs -- build_audit_coverage.record_attempts (95289be5) counts every seat call whether it answers or dies, so the before/after rate is computable from an artifact that already exists. NOT a proposal to slow or block upgrades (L1.28c/L1.21a): model_upgrade.py's evidence-gated adoption is correct and stays; this only makes the post-swap direction observable, and UNMEASURED currently counts as zero (L1.28a).

THE OTHER TWO THIRDS OF R0457 (part (a), list-order, shipped aee2bc86; these two were NOT built and are split so they are not buried by that commit). (b) SILENT PROTOCOL DRIFT IS A GENERATION-SIDE DEFECT CLASS: arXiv 2509.08713 measured 5/20 AI-Scientist-v2 runs quietly subsampling or substituting synthetic data with no report of having done so -- a 25% silent-drift rate. Build: attach a machine-checkable protocol block (universe, date range, n) at GENERATION time and DIFF it at gate time; a mismatch is a defect on the candidate, not a note. Note the desk already has the shape of this elsewhere -- axis_screen bakes its de-contamination gate in rather than trusting the caller -- so this is a known-good pattern applied one stage earlier. (c) TEMPORAL-CUTOFF BACKTEST OF THE GENERATION ORGAN (ForeSci, arXiv 2606.00644, CC-BY, 500 cutoff-aligned research-judgment tasks): score the generator by whether its pre-cutoff judgments TRANSFER, using the desk's own realized ledger as ground truth -- i.e. ask the generator to rank hypotheses as of date T using only pre-T information and compare against what the desk subsequently measured. This is the one instrument that could answer whether the 420/0 campaign was a generator failure or a screen failure, which L1.25's ordered diagnostic (instrument? search space? hypotheses?) currently answers only by elimination. Also carries an evidence-decision decoupling check: whether the organ's stated evidence actually drove its choice. PRIORITISE (b): it is far cheaper, it is a defect-CLOSER rather than a measurement, and 25% is a measured rate on systems of the same shape.

RED TEST AT HEAD, AND IT IS THE SECOND ROT OF THE SAME HAND-MAINTAINED MIRROR IN 24 HOURS. tests/scripts/test_build_standard_contract.py::test_every_governed_organ_meets_the_shared_build_contract fails: set(check_build_standard._GOVERNED) has SIX entries the test's hardcoded GOVERNED literal lacks -- run_cadence.py (5e9db644), check_claim_consistency.py (54bf5a2b), check_citation_integrity.py, check_panel_breadth.py (757c2d79), collect_lending_risk_base_rates.py, run_fee_attribution.py (b3264133) -- all added 2026-08-12/13 by sibling sessions landing L1.61, L1.62, R0425 and R0371. RECORD FORWARD EVIDENCE AS A RATIO AND A LADDER, NOT A SINGLE VERDICT (BRAIN hunter s3, OP-083). WorldQuant BRAIN exposes os.osISSharpeRatio (OOS Sharpe over IS Sharpe) and os.sharpe60/125/250/500 (OOS Sharpe re-measured at four horizons) as first-class queryable metrics; the desk has NEITHER (grep: zero hits for both families across libs/ and scripts/). data/forward_slots.json rows carry only name/kind/source/state -- the two Sharpes whose ratio measures this desk's OWN screen optimism are not persisted anywhere, so the quantity is UNMEASURED and therefore counts as zero (L1.28a). WHY IT PORTS WHERE THE THRESHOLDS DO NOT: brain_calibration.py correctly refuses to let BRAIN's 1.25 Sharpe target become a gate because it is US-equity/daily/dollar-neutral on their conventions -- but a RATIO of two like-measured Sharpes is dimensionless and every one of those conventions cancels. The desk imported the un-portable half and never saw the portable half. WHAT TO BUILD: persist screen (Stage-A) Sharpe and forward Sharpe per candidate, publish the ratio, and re-measure forward Sharpe at 4 cumulative points expressed in OBSERVATIONS not days (L1.48 -- a perp book funding 3x/day accrues evidence ~3x faster than the daily-rebalanced equity book those 60/125/250/500 day-counts came from; copying them as days imports an equity sampling convention as a law). PAYS INTO: L1.29 (the ratio's distribution across the desk's 434 screened candidates is a direct measurement of its own overfitting rate, which nothing currently measures), L1.19/L1.30 (a decay ladder detects an edge dying WHILE it is being confirmed; a single end-of-clock verdict cannot). NOT A BAR CHANGE: this adds no gate, moves no threshold and grants no promotion authority -- it is a measurement duty only.

THE DESK IMPORTED BRAIN'S selfCorrelation CAP AND MISSED ITS prodCorrelation GATE (BRAIN hunter s3, OP-083). BRAIN's alpha API exposes TWO distinct correlation gates: is.selfCorrelation (candidate vs your own prior alphas) and is.prodCorrelation (candidate vs the PRODUCTION book). libs/validation/brain_calibration.py imported only the first, as BRAIN_SELF_CORRELATION_CAP = 0.7; grep finds no candidate-vs-deployed correlation gate anywhere in libs/ or scripts/. THE TWO ASK DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND ONLY ONE PROTECTS THE GROWTH ARGUMENT: selfCorrelation asks 'have I already tried this?', prodCorrelation asks 'does this duplicate what is ALREADY TAKING CAPITAL?' -- two correlated deployed sleeves draw down together, which is exactly what L1.18 (maximum INDEPENDENT compounding sources) exists to prevent. The desk has cohort_independence, effective_bets, panel_breadth and capacity_policy, but nothing that gates a candidate against the DEPLOYED book at promotion time. THE OBVIOUS OBJECTION IS BACKWARDS: the desk runs ~1 deployed sleeve so the gate looks near-vacuous today -- which is precisely why it is cheap now (denominator 1) and binding from the moment the second sleeve lands. Building it after the second sleeve means the first pair is admitted ungated, and that pair is the one that sets the book's correlation floor. CORROBORATED FROM OUTSIDE (OP-084): a measured 50-alpha low-correlation portfolio achieved independence through 49 DISTINCT DATA FIELDS with only 8 operator tokens and 48/50 single-operator expressions -- independence is bought with orthogonal SOURCES, so the gate must be paired with field-count growth, not with more transforms of price. Note the ordering constraint: this gate must read the deployed book at consumption time with a declared max age (L1.44), and must fail toward REFUSING a candidate when the book is unreadable, never toward admitting one.

TMPFS'S DOMINANT PRODUCER BY COUNT IS THE AGENT HARNESS, AND NOTHING REAPS IT. Freeing host-tmpfs-bloated today reclaimed 255 dead agent-session scratch dirs under /tmp/claude-1000 (179MB), the oldest 188h and accumulating continuously since 2026-07-26 -- 316 dirs total. Every desk-side producer of tmpfs has a cleanup owner (run_law_gate reaps its own lawgate-head-* checkouts past 2h; pytest got tmp_path_retention_policy=failed in 513ba24), and this one has none because ITS PRODUCER IS NOT DESK CODE: the Claude Code harness writes each session's task outputs and tool results there and never removes them, so the occupancy R0407 closed keeps returning from outside the repo. max_audit's fence correctly reports rather than deletes (a watcher of a shared resource cannot safely free it) and now names desk-OWNED git worktrees with their reclaim command (268c7f50), but harness scratch carries no ownership evidence the desk can act on automatically. THE SAFE DISCRIMINATOR IS MEASURED AND CHEAP: cron seats run under 'timeout 3000' (50min), so a session dir untouched for >=24h cannot belong to a live session, and a live-holder fd/cwd scan confirmed only 2 of 316 were held. WHAT THIS NEEDS IS A DECISION, NOT A DISCOVERY: either a desk-side janitor with that 24h+no-holder rule (cheap, and the rule is already validated by today's reclaim), or an accepted recurring manual reclaim, or a harness-level retention setting if one exists. Left unfixed the fence will re-fire on a schedule set by agent-session volume, and the failure mode is the R0407 loop: low memory makes an OOM kill likelier, the kill orphans more scratch, the next run starts poorer.

signal_halflife._window_pvalues is ONE-SIDED IN THE POSITIVE DIRECTION (stats.t.sf) and is applied to signals whose IC is negative at both ends, so the decay bar tests a hypothesis whose sign the signal does not have. Measured 2026-08-13: stablecoin_supply has ic_early -0.0199 and ic_recent -0.0260, i.e. every window's p-value is being scored against 'is the IC positive?' when the mechanism's own sign is negative -- so the p-values run high by construction and both halves read ~0.32-0.35 (0.5 is pure null). This does not affect the R0467 verdict (the new null band reads it STABLE either way, and a common sign error is largely differenced out between the halves) but it makes the published error_rate_early / error_rate_late uninterpretable as evidence about THAT signal, and it will matter the moment the bar is asked about a genuinely negative-IC edge. Fix: take the p-value against the signal's PRE-REGISTERED direction, or two-sided, and record which -- never the raw positive tail for every signal. Related unpinned wiring in the same function: stride = ceil(IC_WINDOW/20) hardcodes rolling_ic's step of 20 as a literal, so if that default ever changes the windows silently overlap again and mean-p's independence assumption fails without any test noticing.
